# Shakespeare: characters and their plays — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/shakespeare-plays.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/shakespeare-plays.ttl`](../decks/shakespeare-plays.ttl) · **Cards:** 60 · **Licence:** [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

60 characters from 28 of Shakespeare's plays (tragedies, comedies, romances and two histories), each of whom appears in only one play. Front: the character's name in English and in Swedish (where Swedish has an established form of its own, such as Ofelia, Jago or Botten, that form; otherwise the original name); back: the play, by its English and Swedish title, with a short note on who the character is. Characters whose name is in the play's title are left out. Built from the play texts (Project Gutenberg) and Wikidata, with the Swedish names checked against C. A. Hagberg's translation, and cross-checked against the Folger Shakespeare.

The deck is CC0 1.0. Its content sources are all in the public domain or CC0: the play texts (Shakespeare died in 1616; Project Gutenberg's eBook #100, whose text Project Gutenberg itself says is unrestricted once its licence and trademark are stripped, and nothing of Project Gutenberg's own, neither file nor trademark, is reused); Wikidata (CC0), for the English and Swedish play titles and the Swedish form Ofelia; and C. A. Hagberg's Swedish translation (Hagberg died in 1864; Projekt Runeberg's edition carries no copyright warning), for the Swedish forms Jago, Botten, Benedict, Kardinal Wolsey and Christopher Sluger. The selection of characters is the compiler's own, made by the criteria in the selection and checked mechanically against the play texts; it was not taken from any list. The back notes are the compiler's own wording of the characters' descriptions in the public-domain cast lists. The Folger Digital Texts (CC BY-NC 3.0), the Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) and LIBRIS (terms not readable, recorded as unknown) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts the content sources gave (that a character is in a play and in no other, how Swedish writes a name today, the Swedish titles of editions) and no list or selection was taken from them; three Swedish back notes found to match the Swedish Wikipedia's cast-list wording were reworded (quality-control round 3), and the remaining few-word overlaps are literal translations of the same public-domain cast-list lines; a name or title as such is a fact, not protected expression. Quotations in the provenance report's evidence remain under their sources' licences and are not part of the CC0 deck.

## Method

1. Research, drafting and cross-checking were done by AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic) at Anton Wiklund's direction, with independent AI reviewers and machine checks (the builder's checks against live Wikidata and the app's SHACL/DCAT-AP validators). The cards have not yet been reviewed by a human subject expert.
2. The play texts: Project Gutenberg's Complete Works of William Shakespeare (eBook #100, updated 2025-08-24) was downloaded as plain text (query 1). The script split_plays.py (query 2) split it into its 38 plays using the table of contents (the six poem collections were set aside) and, for each play, extracted the Dramatis Personæ list (36 plays have one; King Richard the Second and The Two Noble Kinsmen have none) and every speech prefix (a line in capitals ending with a full stop).
3. Candidates: a list of 145 well-known leads and supporting roles (146 lines, Shylock twice; recorded verbatim with query 3) was drawn up by the compiler and run through where.py (query 3), which lists for each name every play whose Dramatis Personæ or speech prefixes name it, and every other play whose text merely mentions it. A name qualified only if exactly one play has it as a character. This removed, among others, Claudius (also in Julius Caesar), Edmund (King Lear and three histories), Emilia (four plays), Helena (All's Well and A Midsummer Night's Dream), Demetrius (three plays), Theseus and Hippolyta (also in The Two Noble Kinsmen), Portia (also in Julius Caesar), Antonio and Sebastian (several plays), Angelo and Mariana (two plays each), Valentine (three plays), Brutus (also in Coriolanus), Caius, Pompey, and Falstaff's company (Bardolph, Pistol, Nym, Mistress Quickly, Shallow).
4. Independent check against the Folger edition: fetch_folger.py (query 4) downloaded the character list of all 38 Folger plays (https://www.folgerdigitaltexts.org/<play>/charText/), and verify.py (query 5) required, for every card, that the Gutenberg check and the Folger check both give the card's play and no other (Folger's CamelCase ids such as DromioOfSyracuse were split into words; Folger lists Puck as Robin Goodfellow). This removed Petruchio, whom Folger also lists as a minor speaking character in Romeo and Juliet. The final 60 cards pass both checks; verify.json records the result for each.
5. Every other occurrence of a card's name in the other plays was read (query 6): all are mentions, not characters (e.g. "wise Laertes' son" for Ulysses in Titus Andronicus, "Sir Pandarus of Troy" in The Merry Wives of Windsor, the dead Cassius recalled in Antony and Cleopatra, "Lucio" in the list of guests Capulet invites in Romeo and Juliet), or, for Bottom and Sly, the ordinary English words.
6. Wikidata: queries 7 and 8 listed Shakespeare's works (P50 Q692) with their English and Swedish labels and the characters linked to them by P1441 (present in work); query 9 fetched the labels, aliases and sitelinks of the 28 plays; queries 10 and 11 looked for items for the characters that query 7 did not find (also through the plays' P674); query 12 fetched the labels, aliases and P1441 values of the character items found (47 of them are linked to the card's play and used; the item found for Aaron has no P1441 and is not used); query 13 the death date of Shakespeare. The English and Swedish titles on the backs are the Wikidata labels of the play items.
7. Swedish titles: each Swedish label was compared with the title of the play's Swedish Wikipedia article and its introduction (query 14) and with Swedish editions in LIBRIS (query 15). They agree for all 28 plays kept. LIBRIS found no edition with the exact titles Henrik V, Henrik VIII or Två ungherrar i Verona (Hagberg's titles are Konung Henrik den femte, Konung Henrik den åttonde and Två ungherrar från Verona); for these the Swedish Wikipedia article title, which is also the Wikidata label, was used. Pericles was left out because its Swedish title is not settled: Wikidata has "Perikles" (as the 1986 Swedish edition), Swedish Wikipedia "Pericles" (as the 1931 edition's "Sagospelet Pericles").
8. Swedish names: the front gives the name as Swedish writes it today. For most characters this is the original name. Where Swedish has a form of its own it was taken from a content source and checked against Swedish Wikipedia (query 16, counts of each variant; query 17, the quoted sentences): Ofelia (Wikidata sv label; Swedish Wikipedia 15 times, "Ophelia" 0), Jago (Hagberg; Swedish Wikipedia 32 times, "Iago" 0), Botten (Hagberg; Swedish Wikipedia 11 times; the Wikidata sv label is "Botten Vävare"), Benedict (Hagberg; Swedish Wikipedia 13 times, "Benedick" 0, but also "Benedikt" twice: the majority form, which is also Hagberg's, was kept, as for Rosalind/Rosalinda), Kardinal Wolsey (Hagberg's "Kardinal WOLSEY"; Swedish Wikipedia "kardinal Wolseys", the second sentence naming "kardinal Wolseys", chosen in quality-control round 1 because the first misplaces Wolsey's farewell speech; recorded as "|2" in svquotes.txt) and Christopher Sluger (Hagberg's "CHRISTOPHER SLUGER"; Swedish Wikipedia "fyllot Sluger" once, and "Sly" only in the link "[[Sly (opera)|Sly]]", which query 16 counts as 2, not for the character; adopted in quality-control round 2, the first draft had "Christopher Sly"). Hagberg's 1847–1851 translation (the classic Swedish one, read in Projekt Runeberg's edition, query 18) adapts other names too (Rosalinda, Orsinio, Jachimo, Jessika, Anna Page, Surkart for Dogberry), but the Swedish Wikipedia uses the original names for these (Swedish Wikipedia, following modern translations such as Göran O. Eriksson's), so the cards do too and the evidence records Hagberg's form (the Dogberry note also gives Surkart, which the article mentions). Other characters whose names Swedish translations render as Swedish words were left out (Sir Toby Belch, Hagberg's "Tobias Raap", Swedish Wikipedia's "Tobias Rap"; Sir Andrew Aguecheek, "Andreas Blek av Nosen"; Touchstone, "Proba"; Peter Quince, "Qvitten"/"Kvitten"): these forms come from particular translations and are not in Wikidata, and among translated names (as opposed to spellings) the deck keeps only Botten, which Hagberg, the Swedish Wikipedia and Wikidata's Swedish label all support, and Sluger, Hagberg's form, which the Swedish Wikipedia uses.
9. Every card's character was found in Hagberg's cast list ("Personer") of the same play (query 18; fetch_hagberg.py saved the cast-list pages, evidence_table.py found the line), which also confirms that the Swedish translation has the character in that play.
10. Back notes: each card has a short note on who the character is, written by the compiler from the character's description in the Gutenberg Dramatis Personæ (e.g. "BANQUO, General in the King's Army", "TYBALT, nephew to Lady Capulet"), translated into Swedish by the compiler and compared with Hagberg's description of the same character. Quality-control round 3 compared every Swedish note with the Swedish Wikipedia article on the play (CC BY-SA, verification only; script svoverlap.py, query 20): three notes matched its cast-list wording (Thersites "En vanskapt och hånfull grek", Rosalind "dotter till den äldre hertigen", Apemantus "vresig filosof") and were reworded from the Gutenberg and Hagberg lines ("En missbildad och grovkäftad grek", "Dotter till den landsförvisade hertigen", "En butter filosof"). The overlaps left are three or four words of a literal translation of the same English cast-list line, which any translation would share: "Kung av Skottland" (Duncan), "Lears yngsta dotter" (Cordelia), "förälskad i Lysander" (Hermia), "Hertig av Illyrien" (Orsino), "Kung av Sicilien" (Leontes), "dotter, förälskad i Fenton" (Anne Page), "de två ungherrarna" (Proteus, from the play's title) and the twins' names (Dromio). Five notes add a fact from the play text that the cast list does not give: Tybalt is Lady Capulet's (Fru Capulets) brother's son ("Tybalt, my cousin! O my brother’s child!", Act III, Scene 1; Hagberg's "systerson" is not followed); Wolsey, who has no description in the cast list, is the King's favourite who falls from power (Act III, Scene 2: "Farewell? A long farewell to all my greatness!"); Laertes is Ophelia's brother and Ophelia his sister (both are Polonius's children in the cast list); Lucio is Claudio's friend (he goes to Isabella on Claudio's behalf; Swedish Wikipedia: "Claudios vän Lucio"); Bottom's first name Nick ("Nick Bottom, the weaver" in Act I, Scene 2). English forms of address in the notes are translated as "Fru" (Mistress Page "Fru Page", Lady Capulet "Fru Capulet"; quality-control round 5), since Swedish Wikipedia gives no Swedish form for Lady Capulet and Hagberg's "grefvinnan" is a 19th-century rank not in the English. Kinship words were translated neutrally where English does not say which side: nephew is "nevö" (Benvolio), niece "niece" (Beatrice: the play never says whose daughter she is, so Hagberg's "brorsdotter" is not followed), uncle "onkel".
11. Machine checks: for every card the builder checks against live Wikidata the English and Swedish labels of the play item (the back). For the 47 cards whose character has a Wikidata item linked to the play, it also checks that the item's P1441 (present in work) includes the play, and the item's English label or alias equal to the front, and its Swedish label (or multilingual label) where it equals the Swedish front. Labels not checked, and why: King Duncan (Q15698348, label "King Duncan", no alias "Duncan"), Botten (sv label "Botten Vävare"), Pandarus (sv label "Pandaros", the Homeric form, on an item that is also the figure of the Iliad), and characters with no Swedish label. The deck was then validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (scripts/validate_sources.ts).

## Selection

60 characters from 28 plays: the tragedies Hamlet, Macbeth, Othello, Romeo and Juliet, King Lear, Julius Caesar, Antony and Cleopatra, Coriolanus, Titus Andronicus, Timon of Athens and Troilus and Cressida; the comedies A Midsummer Night's Dream, The Merchant of Venice, Twelfth Night, Much Ado About Nothing, As You Like It, The Taming of the Shrew, Measure for Measure, All's Well That Ends Well, The Comedy of Errors, The Merry Wives of Windsor, Love's Labour's Lost and The Two Gentlemen of Verona; the romances The Tempest, The Winter's Tale and Cymbeline; and the histories Henry V and Henry VIII. Between one and five characters per play, more for the most read plays. A character is included only if (1) exactly one of the 38 plays in the Gutenberg Complete Works has a character of that name, in its cast list or speech prefixes, and the Folger edition agrees; (2) the name is not in the play's title (so no Hamlet, Macbeth, Lady Macbeth, Romeo, Juliet, Lear, Othello, Julius Caesar, Antony, Cleopatra, Coriolanus, Cymbeline, Titus, Troilus, Cressida or Timon; Shylock is kept, since the title is The Merchant of Venice); (3) the character is a lead or a well-known supporting role; (4) the name has one form in current Swedish writing, taken to be the form the Swedish Wikipedia article on the play uses: a Swedish form of its own (Ofelia, Jago, Botten, Benedict, Kardinal Wolsey, Christopher Sluger) or the original name; a form found only in Hagberg's 19th-century translation (Rosalinda, Surkart for Dogberry) does not count, and the back note mentions it where the article does. Left out: characters who recur in several plays (Falstaff, Mistress Quickly, Bardolph, Pistol, Nym, Shallow) or share a name with a character of another play (see the method); the history plays King John, Richard II, Richard III and Henry IV and VI, whose Swedish titles are not settled (Wikidata has Rickard II and Rikard III, Swedish Wikipedia Richard II, Richard III and Kung John against Wikidata's Kung Johan; Henry IV, Part 2 has no Swedish label) and whose figures often recur; Pericles, whose Swedish title is not settled (Perikles or Pericles); The Two Noble Kinsmen (co-written with John Fletcher, not in the First Folio, and with no Swedish title of its own); Edward III, which the Gutenberg Complete Works does not include. Characters whose speech prefix or cast-list name is not their name (Feste is "Clown" in the Gutenberg cast list) or who never appear on stage (Sycorax, Yorick) were also left out. Isabella (Measure for Measure) was left out because Hagberg's Swedish translation calls the Queen of France in Henry V Isabella as well.

## Queries

**1. Download the Complete Works (eBook #100) as plain text** (The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (Project Gutenberg eBook #100, most recently updated August 24, 2025))

```
curl -sL -H "User-Agent: solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o pg100.txt https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/100/pg100.txt
```

**2. Split the eBook into its plays and index each play's Dramatis Personæ and speech prefixes (python3 split_plays.py; writes plays.json)** (The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (Project Gutenberg eBook #100, most recently updated August 24, 2025))

```
"""Split Project Gutenberg eBook #100 (pg100.txt) into its plays and index each
play's Dramatis Personae and speech prefixes. Writes plays.json."""
import json, re
from pathlib import Path

D = Path(__file__).parent
text = (D / "pg100.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
body = text.split("*** START OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK")[1].split("*** END OF THE PROJECT GUTENBERG EBOOK")[0]
lines = body.splitlines()

# The contents list (indented titles), in order.
start = next(i for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.strip() == "Contents")
titles = []
for l in lines[start + 1:]:
    if not l.strip():
        if titles:
            break
        continue
    titles.append(l.strip())

# Each work begins at the first line equal to its title after the contents.
pos = start + len(titles) + 2
starts = []
for t in titles:
    i = next(j for j in range(pos, len(lines)) if lines[j].strip() == t)
    starts.append(i)
    pos = i + 1
starts.append(len(lines))

POEMS = {"THE SONNETS", "A LOVER’S COMPLAINT", "THE PASSIONATE PILGRIM", "THE PHOENIX AND THE TURTLE",
         "THE RAPE OF LUCRECE", "VENUS AND ADONIS"}
plays = {}
for t, a, b in zip(titles, starts, starts[1:]):
    if t in POEMS:
        continue
    seg = lines[a:b]
    # Dramatis Personae block: from the heading to the first "ACT I"/"INDUCTION"/"PROLOGUE" heading.
    dp_start = next((k for k, l in enumerate(seg) if l.strip().lower().startswith("dramatis person")), None)
    dp = []
    if dp_start is not None:
        for l in seg[dp_start + 1:]:
            s = l.strip()
            if re.match(r"^(ACT I\b|INDUCTION|PROLOGUE|THE PROLOGUE|ACT 1)", s):
                break
            if s:
                dp.append(s)
    prefixes = sorted({l.strip()[:-1] for l in seg if re.match(r"^[A-Z][A-Z’' .,-]+\.$", l.strip())
                       and not re.match(r"^(ACT|SCENE|EPILOGUE|PROLOGUE|INDUCTION)\b", l.strip())})
    plays[t] = {"lines": [a, b], "dramatisPersonae": dp, "speechPrefixes": prefixes, "text": "\n".join(seg)}

(D / "plays.json").write_text(json.dumps(plays, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
for t, p in plays.items():
    print(f"{t}: {len(p['dramatisPersonae'])} DP lines, {len(p['speechPrefixes'])} prefixes")
```

**3. For each candidate name (candidates.txt, 145 names; its contents are recorded as query 3a below), the plays that have it as a character and the plays that only mention it (python3 where.py)** (The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (Project Gutenberg eBook #100, most recently updated August 24, 2025))

```
"""For each name given on the command line (or in candidates.txt), list the plays of
Gutenberg #100 whose Dramatis Personae or speech prefixes name it, and every play whose
text mentions it (whole word, case-insensitive), with counts."""
import json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

D = Path(__file__).parent
plays = json.loads((D / "plays.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
names = sys.argv[1:] or [l.strip() for l in (D / "candidates.txt").read_text().splitlines() if l.strip()]
short = lambda t: re.sub(r"^(THE TRAGEDY OF |THE LIFE OF |THE LIFE AND DEATH OF )", "", t)
for n in names:
    pat = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])" + re.escape(n) + r"(?![a-z])", re.I)
    role, mention = [], []
    for t, p in plays.items():
        inrole = any(pat.search(x) for x in p["dramatisPersonae"]) or any(pat.search(x) for x in p["speechPrefixes"])
        c = len(pat.findall(p["text"]))
        if inrole:
            role.append(f"{short(t)}({c})")
        elif c:
            mention.append(f"{short(t)}({c})")
    flag = "OK " if len(role) == 1 else "XX "
    print(f"{flag}{n}: ROLE {role}  MENTION {mention}")
```

**4. Download the character lists of all 38 Folger plays (python3 fetch_folger.py)** (Folger Digital Texts: character lists of the plays (charText, words spoken per character))

```
"""Fetch the Folger Digital Texts character lists (words spoken per character) of all 38 plays:
https://www.folgerdigitaltexts.org/<code>/charText/ -> folger/<code>.html, and folger_chars.json."""
import json, re, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
CODES = "AWW Ant AYL Err Cor Cym Ham 1H4 2H4 H5 1H6 2H6 3H6 H8 JC Jn Lr LLL Mac MM MV Wiv MND Ado Oth Per R2 R3 Rom Shr Tmp Tim Tit Tro TN TGV TNK WT".split()
H = Path(__file__).parent
D = H / "folger"
D.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
chars = {}
for c in CODES:
    url = f"https://www.folgerdigitaltexts.org/{c}/charText/"
    with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=60) as r:
        h = r.read().decode("utf-8")
    (D / f"{c}.html").write_text(h, encoding="utf-8")
    chars[c] = [(int(w), n) for w, n in re.findall(r'width: 60px;">(\d+)</div><div style="float:left;"><a href="[^"]*">([^<]*)</a>', h)]
    print(c, len(chars[c]))
    time.sleep(0.5)
(H / "folger_chars.json").write_text(json.dumps(chars, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
```

**5. Check every card against both the Gutenberg plays and the Folger lists (python3 verify.py; cards.json holds the 60 cards: id, English and Swedish front, play, search name, Wikidata item)** (The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (Project Gutenberg eBook #100, most recently updated August 24, 2025))

```
"""For every card in cards.json: the plays of Gutenberg #100 whose Dramatis Personae or speech prefixes
name the character, and the Folger plays whose character list names it (whole word, case-insensitive).
Both must be exactly the card's play. Writes verify.json (evidence) and prints a summary."""
import json, re
from pathlib import Path

H = Path(__file__).parent
spec = json.loads((H / "cards.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
plays = json.loads((H / "plays.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
folger = json.loads((H / "folger_chars.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
pg_to_q = {p["pg"]: q for q, p in spec["plays"].items()}
fo_to_q = {p["folger"]: q for q, p in spec["plays"].items()}
FOLGER_TOKEN = {"puck": "Robin Goodfellow"}  # Folger's name for Puck
out = {}
bad = 0
for cid, en, sv, q, token, wd in spec["cards"]:
    pat = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])" + re.escape(token) + r"(?![a-z])", re.I)
    pg_roles, pg_dp, pg_mentions = [], None, {}
    for t, p in plays.items():
        dp = [x for x in p["dramatisPersonae"] if pat.search(x)]
        sp = [x for x in p["speechPrefixes"] if pat.search(x)]
        n = len(pat.findall(p["text"]))
        if dp or sp:
            pg_roles.append(t)
            if pg_to_q.get(t) == q:
                pg_dp = {"dramatisPersonae": dp, "speechPrefixes": sp, "occurrences": n}
        elif n:
            pg_mentions[t] = n
    # Folger ids are CamelCase ("DromioOfSyracuse", "RobinGoodfellow"): split them into words first.
    fpat = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])" + re.escape(FOLGER_TOKEN.get(cid, token)) + r"(?![a-z])", re.I)
    split = lambda nm: re.sub(r"(?<=[a-z])(?=[A-Z])", " ", nm)
    fo_roles = {c: [(w, nm) for w, nm in chars if fpat.search(split(nm))] for c, chars in folger.items()}
    fo_roles = {c: v for c, v in fo_roles.items() if v}
    ok_pg = len(pg_roles) == 1 and pg_to_q.get(pg_roles[0]) == q
    ok_fo = len(fo_roles) == 1 and fo_to_q.get(next(iter(fo_roles))) == q
    out[cid] = {"pgRolePlays": pg_roles, "pg": pg_dp, "pgMentionsElsewhere": pg_mentions, "folger": fo_roles,
                "ok": ok_pg and ok_fo}
    if not (ok_pg and ok_fo):
        bad += 1
    print(f"{'OK ' if ok_pg and ok_fo else 'XX '}{cid}: PG {pg_roles} | Folger {fo_roles} | elsewhere {pg_mentions}")
(H / "verify.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
print("problems:", bad)
```

**10a. wdsearch.py, the wbsearchentities script of query 10, verbatim** (Wikidata: the plays of William Shakespeare (Q692) and their characters (P1441 present in work), with English and Swedish labels)

```
"""Search Wikidata (wbsearchentities, en) for each name; print id, label, description. Saves wdsearch.json."""
import json, sys, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
H = Path(__file__).parent
res = {}
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    url = "https://www.wikidata.org/w/api.php?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(
        {"action": "wbsearchentities", "search": name, "language": "en", "limit": 8, "format": "json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=60) as r:
        data = json.load(r)
    res[name] = {"url": url, "search": data.get("search", [])}
    print("==", name)
    for s in data.get("search", []):
        print("  ", s["id"], s.get("label"), "—", s.get("description", ""))
    time.sleep(0.3)
p = H / "wdsearch.json"
old = json.loads(p.read_text()) if p.exists() else {}
old.update(res)
p.write_text(json.dumps(old, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
```

**13. Shakespeare's death date (q7.rq). Its second UNION branch, meant to find Carl August Hagberg's death date, matched nothing (a label-based lookup); Hagberg's item Q346056 was found by query 10, and his death date was confirmed by query 13b** (Wikidata: the plays of William Shakespeare (Q692) and their characters (P1441 present in work), with English and Swedish labels)

```
SELECT ?person ?label ?death WHERE {
  VALUES ?person { wd:Q692 }

  UNION
  { ?h rdfs:label "Carl August Hagberg"@sv ; wdt:P570 ?death . BIND(?h AS ?person2) BIND("Carl August Hagberg" AS ?label) BIND(?h AS ?person) }
}
```

**14. Current wikitext and revision id of the Swedish Wikipedia articles on the plays (python3 fetch_wiki.py sv svwiki <titles>)** (Svenskspråkiga Wikipedia: the articles on the plays (Hamlet, Othello, En midsommarnattsdröm, Mycket väsen för ingenting, Som ni behagar, Cymbeline, Trettondagsafton (pjäs), Muntra fruarna i Windsor, Henrik VIII (pjäs), Lika för lika, Köpmannen i Venedig and others))

```
"""Fetch the current wikitext (with revision id) of Wikipedia articles via the MediaWiki API.
usage: fetch_wiki.py <lang> <outdir> <title>...   -> <outdir>/<title>.json"""
import json, sys, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
lang, outdir, titles = sys.argv[1], Path(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3:]
outdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for t in titles:
    url = (f"https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&rvprop=ids|content"
           f"&rvslots=main&format=json&formatversion=2&redirects=1&titles=" + urllib.parse.quote(t))
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        data = json.load(r)
    page = data["query"]["pages"][0]
    rev = page.get("revisions", [{}])[0]
    out = {"title": page.get("title"), "revid": rev.get("revid"), "url": url,
           "content": rev.get("slots", {}).get("main", {}).get("content", "")}
    (outdir / (t.replace("/", "_") + ".json")).write_text(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    print(t, "->", out["title"], out["revid"], len(out["content"]))
    time.sleep(0.5)

# titles: "En midsommarnattsdröm" "Slutet gott, allting gott" "Antonius och Cleopatra" "Som ni behagar" "Coriolanus (pjäs)" "Cymbeline" "Hamlet" "Henrik V (pjäs)" "Henrik VIII (pjäs)" "Julius Caesar (pjäs)" "Kung Lear" "Kärt besvär förgäves" "Macbeth" "Lika för lika" "Mycket väsen för ingenting" "Othello" "Pericles (pjäs)" "Romeo och Julia" "Förvillelser (pjäs)" "Köpmannen i Venedig" "Muntra fruarna i Windsor" "Så tuktas en argbigga" "Stormen" "Två ungherrar i Verona" "En vintersaga" "Timon av Aten" "Titus Andronicus" "Troilus och Cressida" "Trettondagsafton (pjäs)" "William Shakespeare" "Richard II (pjäs)" "Richard III (pjäs)" "Kung John"
```

```
"""Search LIBRIS (xsearch API) for Swedish-language Shakespeare editions of each title in libris.txt
and save the raw JSON; print count and the titles/years found."""
import json, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
H = Path(__file__).parent
out = H / "libris"
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
for title in [l.strip() for l in (H / "libris.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if l.strip()]:
    q = f'tit:"{title}" förf:Shakespeare spr:swe'
    url = "https://libris.kb.se/xsearch?" + urllib.parse.urlencode({"query": q, "format": "json", "n": 200})
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        data = json.load(r)
    (out / f"{title}.json").write_text(json.dumps({"url": url, "data": data}, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
    recs = data.get("xsearch", {}).get("list", [])
    n = data.get("xsearch", {}).get("records")
    titles = sorted({(str(r.get("title", "")), str(r.get("date", ""))) for r in recs}, key=lambda x: x[1])
    print(f"{title}: {n} records; e.g. {titles[:3]} … {titles[-3:]}")
    time.sleep(1)
```

**17. The sentence or cast-list line quoted for a Swedish form (python3 svquotes.py; spec svquotes.txt); since quality-control round 4 a spec line may name which matching sentence to take (n), so that the hand-picked Wolsey quote of round 1 is reproducible** (Svenskspråkiga Wikipedia: the articles on the plays (Hamlet, Othello, En midsommarnattsdröm, Mycket väsen för ingenting, Som ni behagar, Cymbeline, Trettondagsafton (pjäs), Muntra fruarna i Windsor, Henrik VIII (pjäs), Lika för lika, Köpmannen i Venedig and others))

```
"""Extract, from the fetched sv.wikipedia wikitext, the n-th sentence or list line naming a word (wiki markup
stripped to plain text as displayed; n = 1 unless given). Spec: svquotes.txt 'card|article|word[|n]'.
Writes svquotes.json."""
import json, re
from pathlib import Path

H = Path(__file__).parent
D = H / "svwiki"

def plain(s):
    s = re.sub(r"(?s)<ref[^>]*/>|<ref.*?</ref>", "", s)
    s = re.sub(r"\[\[(?:[^|\]]*\|)?([^\]]*)\]\]", r"\1", s)
    s = re.sub(r"'''?", "", s)
    return s

out = {}
for line in (H / "svquotes.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    if not line.strip():
        continue
    cid, art, word, *n = line.split("|")
    n = int(n[0]) if n else 1
    a = json.loads((D / f"{art}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    text = plain(a["content"])
    pieces = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+|\n", text)
    hits = [p.strip() for p in pieces if re.search(r"(?<![\wåäö])" + re.escape(word) + r"(?![a-zåäö])", p)]
    hit = hits[n - 1] if len(hits) >= n else None
    out[cid] = {"article": a["title"], "revid": a["revid"], "word": word, "n": n, "quote": hit}
    print(cid, a["revid"], "::", hit)
(H / "svquotes.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
```

**18.
```
"""Fetch the volume indexes of Projekt Runeberg's Hagberg edition (https://runeberg.org/hagberg/a/ ... l/),
save them, and fetch every page whose table-of-contents entry is "Personer" (the dramatis personae)."""
import html, re, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
D = Path(__file__).parent / "hagberg"
D.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

def get(url):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
        raw = r.read()
    for enc in ("utf-8", "latin-1"):
        try:
            return raw.decode(enc)
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            pass

def text(h):
    h = re.sub(r"(?s)<script.*?</script>|<style.*?</style>", " ", h)
    return re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", h)))

for vol in "abcdefghijkl":
    idx = get(f"https://runeberg.org/hagberg/{vol}/")
    (D / f"{vol}_index.html").write_text(idx, encoding="utf-8")
    # entries like <a href="0003.html">Personer</a> preceded by the play title
    links = [(h, t.strip()) for h, t in re.findall(r"<a href=\"(\d{4}\.html)\"\s+style=[^>]*>([^<]*)</a>", idx)]
    print(vol, [(h, t) for h, t in links if "erson" in t or "Pers" in t][:20])
    for h, t in links:
        if "erson" in t:
            for n in (int(h[:4]), int(h[:4]) + 1):  # the list and the page after it
                page = get(f"https://runeberg.org/hagberg/{vol}/{n:04d}.html")
                (D / f"{vol}_{n:04d}.html").write_text(page, encoding="utf-8")
                time.sleep(0.5)
    time.sleep(0.5)

"""Collect, per card, the evidence lines: Gutenberg Dramatis Personae line, Folger character-list entry,
and the line of Hagberg's Personer list (Runeberg) naming the character. Writes evidence_table.json."""
import html, json, re
from pathlib import Path

H = Path(__file__).parent
spec = json.loads((H / "cards.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
ver = json.loads((H / "verify.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
HAGBERG_FORM = {"ophelia": "OPHELIA", "iago": "JAGO", "benedick": "BENEDICT", "bottom": "BOTTEN", "wolsey": "WOLSEY",
                "rosalind": "ROSALINDA", "dogberry": "SURKART", "iachimo": "JACHIMO", "anne-page": "ANNA PAGE",
                "christopher-sly": "CHRISTOPHER SLUGER", "orsino": "ORSINIO", "jessica": "JESSIKA", "cassio": "CASSIO", "duncan": "DUNCAN"}
pages = {}
for p in sorted((H / "hagberg").glob("?_0*.html")):
    h = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    t = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", h))
    i = t.lower().find("personer")
    if i < 0:
        continue
    pages[p.name] = [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", l).strip() for l in t[i:i + 4000].splitlines() if l.strip()]
out = {}
for cid, en, sv, q, token, wd in spec["cards"]:
    form = HAGBERG_FORM.get(cid, token.upper())
    hits = [(f, l) for f, ls in pages.items() for l in ls[:60] if re.search(r"(?<![A-ZÅÄÖ])" + re.escape(form) + r"(?![A-ZÅÄÖ])", l)]
    v = ver[cid]
    out[cid] = {"pgDP": (v["pg"] or {}).get("dramatisPersonae"), "pgPrefixes": (v["pg"] or {}).get("speechPrefixes"),
                "pgOccurrences": (v["pg"] or {}).get("occurrences"), "folger": v["folger"], "hagberg": hits[:3]}
    print(cid, "| PG:", out[cid]["pgDP"][:1] if out[cid]["pgDP"] else out[cid]["pgPrefixes"], "| F:", list(v["folger"].values())[0][:1], "| H:", hits[:2])
(H / "evidence_table.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
```

```
"""Fetch the licence/terms pages of the sources and print the sentences that state the terms."""
import html, re, time, urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

UA = "Mozilla/5.0 (solid-memo deck research; https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"
H = Path(__file__).parent / "terms"
H.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
PAGES = {
    "gutenberg_license": ("https://www.gutenberg.org/policy/license.html", ["public domain", "trademark", "Royalty"]),
    "gutenberg_permission": ("https://www.gutenberg.org/policy/permission.html", ["public domain", "trademark", "remove"]),
    "runeberg_copyright": ("https://runeberg.org/admin/copyright.html", ["fri", "free", "upphovsr", "copyright"]),
    "wikidata_licensing": ("https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Licensing", ["Creative Commons Zero"]),
    "libris": ("https://www.kb.se/samverkan-och-utveckling/libris/att-anvanda-librisdata.html", ["Creative Commons", "fritt tillgängliga"]),
    "svwiki_hamlet": ("https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamlet", ["Creative Commons"]),
    "runeberg_hagberg": ("https://runeberg.org/hagberg/", ["Hagberg"]),
}
for key, (url, words) in PAGES.items():
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA}), timeout=60) as r:
            raw = r.read()
    except Exception as e:
        print("==", key, url, "ERROR", e)
        continue
    (H / f"{key}.html").write_bytes(raw)
    t = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    t = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", re.sub(r"(?s)<script.*?</script>|<style.*?</style>", "", t))))
    print("==", key, url, len(t))
    seen = 0
    for w in words:
        for m in re.finditer(re.escape(w), t, re.I):
            print("   …" + t[max(0, m.start() - 250): m.end() + 250] + "…")
            seen += 1
            if seen > 4:
                break
    time.sleep(0.5)
```

**20. Quality control, round 3: every Swedish back note compared with the Swedish Wikipedia article on the card's play (python3 svoverlap.py authored/shakespeare-plays.json, on the wikitext saved by query 14)** (Svenskspråkiga Wikipedia: the articles on the plays (Hamlet, Othello, En midsommarnattsdröm, Mycket väsen för ingenting, Som ni behagar, Cymbeline, Trettondagsafton (pjäs), Muntra fruarna i Windsor, Henrik VIII (pjäs), Lika för lika, Köpmannen i Venedig and others))

```
"""For every card's Swedish back note, the longest stretch of it (in words) that also occurs in the
Swedish Wikipedia article on the card's play (wikitext with links/markup stripped, case-insensitive)."""
import json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

H = Path(__file__).parent.parent
dossier = Path(sys.argv[1])
d = json.loads(dossier.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
art = {}
for f in (H / "svwiki").glob("*.json"):
    t = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["content"]
    t = re.sub(r"\[\[(?:[^|\]]*\|)?([^\]]*)\]\]", r"\1", t)
    t = re.sub(r"'{2,}", "", t)
    art[f.stem] = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", t.lower())


def words(s):
    return re.findall(r"\w+", s.lower())


for c in d["cards"]:
    note = (c.get("backNote") or {}).get("sv")
    if not note:
        continue
    sv_title = c["back"]["sv"]
    cands = [k for k in art if k == sv_title or k.startswith(sv_title + " (")]
    best = ""
    w = words(note)
    for k in cands:
        a = " ".join(words(art[k]))
        for i in range(len(w)):
            for j in range(len(w), i, -1):
                s = " ".join(w[i:j])
                if len(s) > len(best) and re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(s) + r"\b", a):
                    best = s
                    break
    flag = "  <==" if len(best.split()) >= 3 else ""
    print(f"{c['id']:20} {note!r:60} longest shared: {best!r}{flag}")
```

## Quality control

6 rounds, 40 findings: 28 fixed, 2 rejected after checking, 10 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (235 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources, licences and machine checks: every card's character against the cast lists and speech prefixes of all 38 Gutenberg plays and the character lists of all 38 Folger plays; the Swedish names against Wikidata, Hagberg's translation and the Swedish Wikipedia; the Swedish titles against Wikidata, the Swedish Wikipedia and LIBRIS. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 60 cards, the sources and the deck metadata.

All 60 characters are characters of exactly one play in both the Gutenberg and the Folger texts, and every one is in Hagberg's cast list of the same play. The English and Swedish play titles are the Wikidata labels and agree with the Swedish Wikipedia; the builder's Wikidata checks cover the back of every card and, for the 47 characters with a Wikidata item, the character's link to the play and its labels. No Wikidata check was skipped because Wikidata disagreed with a better source; label checks were left out only where the card deliberately uses another form (listed below). One candidate failed the Folger check and several were dropped for unsettled Swedish names or titles.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| petruchio (dropped) | Gutenberg has Petruchio as a character only in The Taming of the Shrew, but the Folger character list of Romeo and Juliet has a "Petruchio" (2 words); in the Gutenberg text of Romeo and Juliet the Nurse points out "young Petruchio" at Capulet's feast. | Petruchio left out (the front would have two answers); Christopher Sly represents The Taming of the Shrew. | fixed |
| isabella (dropped) | Isabella is a character only in Measure for Measure in English, but Hagberg's Swedish cast list of Henry V names the Queen of France "ISABELLA" (English "Isabel"), so the Swedish front would not be unique. | Left out; Lucio represents Measure for Measure. | fixed |
| marina (dropped) | Pericles' Swedish title is not settled: Wikidata sv label "Perikles" (as the 1986 edition), Swedish Wikipedia "Pericles (pjäs)" (as the 1931 edition's "Sagospelet Pericles"). | Pericles left out rather than choose one title. | fixed |
| charmian (dropped) | Hagberg calls Cleopatra's attendant "CHARMIANA"; Swedish Wikipedia does not name her, so today's Swedish form could not be confirmed. | Left out; Enobarbus represents Antony and Cleopatra. | fixed |
| feste (dropped) | The Gutenberg cast list and speech prefixes call Olivia's fool "CLOWN"; the name Feste occurs once in the text. | Left out. | fixed |
| bottom | Wikidata's sv label of Nick Bottom (Q2190927) is "Botten Vävare", not "Botten". | Front "Botten", Hagberg's form ("BOTTEN, väfvare.") and the one Swedish Wikipedia uses ("Niklas Botten, vävare"); the sv label check is left out, the English alias "Bottom" and P1441 are checked. | no change needed |
| pandarus | Wikidata Q1057384 is both the Homeric Pandarus and Shakespeare's (P1441 the Iliad and Troilus and Cressida); its sv label is "Pandaros", the Greek form. | Front "Pandarus" in Swedish too (Hagberg's "PANDARUS", Swedish Wikipedia "Pandarus" 7 times, "Pandaros" 0 in the article on the play); sv label check left out. | no change needed |
| duncan | Wikidata Q15698348's English label is "King Duncan", with no alias "Duncan". | Front "Duncan" as in the cast list ("DUNCAN, King of Scotland."); P1441 checked, label not. | no change needed |
| iago | Wikidata Q1655364 has no Swedish label. | Swedish "Jago" from Hagberg ("JAGO. hans fänrik."), confirmed by the Swedish Wikipedia article on Othello (Jago 32 times, Iago 0). | no change needed |
| aaron | The only Wikidata item found for Aaron (Q73007104, "fictional character") has no P1441. | Not used; the card relies on Gutenberg, Folger and Hagberg, and the play labels are checked. | no change needed |
| rosalind | Hagberg writes "ROSALINDA" (likewise Orsinio, Jachimo, Jessika, Anna Page, Christopher Sluger, and Surkart for Dogberry). | The cards use the original names, which today's Swedish uses (Swedish Wikipedia: Rosalind 43 times, Rosalinda once; Orsino, Iachimo, Jessica, Anne Page, Dogberry "(Surkart i Carl August Hagbergs översättning)"); Hagberg's forms are recorded in the evidence. (Sluger was later adopted for the Swedish front, see round 2.) | no change needed |
| proteus | The Swedish title of The Two Gentlemen of Verona varies (Två ungherrar i Verona, Två ungherrar från Verona, Två gentlemän från Verona, Två herrar från Verona); LIBRIS has no edition with the exact title of the Wikidata label. | Back "Två ungherrar i Verona", the Wikidata label and the Swedish Wikipedia article title (whose introduction gives the other titles). Kept, since the card's answer is the play and any of these titles names it. | no change needed |
| lucio | "Lucio" also occurs once in Romeo and Juliet, in the letter listing Capulet's guests. | A name in a list, not a character: neither Gutenberg nor Folger has a Lucio in that play. Kept. | no change needed |
| puck | Folger lists Puck under his other name, Robin Goodfellow. | The Folger check used that name; the Gutenberg cast list reads "PUCK, or ROBIN GOODFELLOW, a Fairy" and the note gives the other name. | no change needed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 60 cards: every character re-checked against the character lists of all 38 Folger plays (fetched live by the reviewer), the play labels against live Wikidata, and every back note against the Dramatis Personæ and Hagberg's cast lists.

No wrong card. The reviewer's own scan of the Folger lists found every character in exactly one play, the play on the card's back; the Wikidata labels of all 28 plays agree with the backs; the builder's 235 checks pass. Two warnings (the Swedish Bottom note used the English name; the Dromio evidence said 39 plays) and three suggestions. Three findings were fixed and two suggestions declined.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| bottom | The Swedish back note "Vävaren Nick Bottom." uses the English name, while the Swedish front is "Botten" (Hagberg "BOTTEN, väfvare."; Swedish Wikipedia "Niklas Botten, vävare"). | Swedish note changed to "Vävaren Botten (Nick Bottom i originalet).", which keeps the front's Swedish form and links it to the original name; the English note is unchanged. | fixed |
| dromio | The Gutenberg evidence said "Of the 39 plays in the eBook"; the eBook has 38 plays, as the method and every other card say. | Corrected to "Of the 38 plays". The fact itself was right (verify.json: Dromio is a character only in The Comedy of Errors). | fixed |
| wolsey | The Swedish Wikipedia sentence quoted to show the form "kardinal Wolsey" puts Wolsey's speech after his fall in act five; the speech ("Farewell? A long farewell to all my greatness!") is in Act III, Scene 2. | Confirmed in the Gutenberg text (the speech follows the heading "SCENE II. Ante-chamber to the King’s apartment." under ACT III). The quote was replaced by another sentence of the same revision that shows the form without the error: "Pjäsen börjar med att Buckingham … beklagar sig över kardinal Wolseys hänsynslösa och övermodiga styre." | fixed |
| beatrice | Suggests the Swedish note "Leonatos brorsdotter." (Hagberg's wording) instead of "Leonatos niece.", taking Beatrice to be the daughter of Leonato's brother Antonio. | Rejected. The play never says whose daughter Beatrice is: the cast list says only "Niece to Leonato", and in Act V, Scene 1 Leonato says "My brother hath a daughter, / Almost the copy of my child that’s dead", a daughter who is not Beatrice (she turns out to be Hero), so Beatrice is not shown to be Antonio's daughter. "Brorsdotter" would add a claim the text does not make; "niece" is a Swedish word (SAOL) and keeps the English neutrality, as method step 10 records. | rejected |
| imogen | Optionally mention that some modern editions (Oxford, RSC) call her "Innogen". | Declined. The card is correct, and all the deck's sources (Gutenberg, Folger, Hagberg, Wikidata Q6005653, which has no alias "Innogen", checked 2026-10-04) use "Imogen"; adding the variant would need a further source for the editions that use it, for a fact that is not needed to answer the card. | rejected |

### Round 2: Language, translation and language tags (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Language, translation and language tags reviewer · **Scope:** All 60 cards in both languages, the title, the description and the keywords, and the language tags of the built deck.

All card text is tagged @en/@sv; the 28 Swedish titles match the Wikidata sv labels and the Swedish Wikipedia.
